name: Buraco Brazilian
description: Buraco (also known as Canastra, Biriba, or Perida) is a four-player partnership card game from Brazil related to Canasta. Players meld sequences of three or more consecutive cards of a suit, aiming to create canastas (sequences of 7+ cards). The game uses two 52-card decks with four jokers (108 cards total).

overview.description: Buraco (also known as Canastra, Biriba, or Perida) is a four-player partnership card game from Brazil related to Canasta. Players meld sequences of three or more consecutive cards of a suit, aiming to create canastas (sequences of 7+ cards). The game uses two 52-card decks with four jokers (108 cards total).

history.origins: Buraco originated in the Rio de la Plata region of South America (Argentina and Uruguay) in the 1940s and remains widely played in Brazil. It is closely related to Canasta and similar to Samba in its melding mechanics. In Brazil the game is also known as Canastra, Biriba, or Perida in different regions.
timeline: Mid-late 20th century: Became popular throughout Brazil
1990s: Italian variation Burraco became extremely popular in Italy
Modern era: Digital versions and online play available
history.cultural: Buraco is one of the most popular card games in Brazil, commonly played socially and in clubs. The game has regional variations including Buraco Aberto (open) and Buraco Fechado (closed).
history.evolution: The game evolved from Canasta with unique features like the morto (extra hand) mechanic. A similar game Burako is played in Argentina using tiles instead of cards. Since the 1990s, the Italian variation Burraco has gained massive popularity.

setup.players: 4 players in two fixed partnerships (partners sit opposite)
setup.deck: 108-card pack: two standard 52-card decks plus four wild jokers (curingÃ£o). Twos (curinga) can be used as wild cards or natural twos.
setup.dealing: Player to dealer's right cuts and forms two 11-card piles (mortos) set aside. Dealer deals 11 cards to each player from remaining pack. Remaining 42 cards form draw pile (monte). Discard pile (lixo/bagaÃ§o) starts empty.

rules.objective: Be the first team to reach 3000 points by melding sequences, creating canastas (7+ card sequences), and going out. Score points from melded cards plus bonuses for canastas.
rules.gameplay: First player (to dealer's right) draws top card, decides to keep or discard it, then may meld and must discard. Play proceeds counter-clockwise. Each turn: draw from stock or take entire discard pile; optionally meld or add to team melds; discard one card. First player to empty hand takes a morto (11-card extra hand). Second morto goes to first player of other team who runs out. Team can end play with second batida if they have a clean canastra (7+ cards without wild).
keyRules: 108 cards: 2 decks + 4 jokers; twos are wild
Two 11-card mortos set aside for first players out
Melds are sequences of 3+ consecutive cards of a suit
Aces rank high and low: A-2-3-...-Q-K-A possible
Max one wild card per sequence
Canastra = sequence of 7+ cards (clean or dirty)
Need clean canastra to go out

strategy.basic: Prioritize creating your first canastra early. Save wild cards (jokers and twos) for completing sequences. Watch which cards your partner is collecting. Take the discard pile only when it helps complete valuable melds.
strategy.intermediate: Track which cards have been played to predict what opponents hold. Coordinate with partner on which sequences to build. Time your batida carefully - taking a morto gives more cards but may help opponents. Consider vulnerability status when planning initial melds.
strategy.advanced: Calculate risk vs reward when taking the discard pile (opponents see what you take). Manage wild cards strategically - they complete sequences but reduce canastra value. Force opponents to take mortos at disadvantageous times. In endgame, block opponents from completing canastras while setting up your own go-out.
tips: Always try to create at least one clean canastra for going out
Save wild cards for critical sequence completions
Watch partner's discards to understand their hand
Taking a morto after discarding (batida indireta) delays using it
Going out quickly can deny opponents their morto bonus
Vulnerable teams need 75+ points for first meld
A canastra real (14-card clean sequence) scores 1000 bonus points

scoring.description: Scoring uses point values per card plus bonuses for canastras: clean (no wild) sequences of seven or more cards score 200 points, dirty sequences with a wild score 100 points, clean 13-card sequences score 500 points, clean 14-card sequences score 1000 points, and going out scores 100 points; card values from Pagat are added for melded cards and subtracted for cards left in hand, with penalties for unused mortos.
scoring.winCondition: First team to reach the target score (typically 3,000 points) wins; higher cumulative score wins.
